answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may vote on shared tasks, then slash that bond when a randomly sampled audit proves its reports were fabricated. Auditors compare claims with signed task receipts, so copying a crowd’s answers does not establish independent work. The karst ledger records bonds and penalties; a whisper channel can flag suspicious clusters, while umber marks unresolved cases. A sybil attacker must lock real capital per identity and risks losing it, making a large fake swarm costly rather than free.
